headline: The Top Five Cashed And The Other Thirty Three Set Money On Fire
paragraphs: Thirty eight tickets went out at ten dollars each from twenty nine games, with forty one games left alone. The result was 13-25, a loss of $133.51, and an ROI of negative 35.1 percent. The model walked in expecting to hit 57.5 percent and hit 34.2 percent instead, which is the kind of gap that stops being variance and starts being a personality.

The spread card did the damage: 8-17 and down $97.28 across twenty five plays. Totals were almost respectable at 4-5. The moneyline went 1-3 while projecting a tidy 65 percent, and the centerpiece of that wreckage was Massachusetts -3, a 77 percent conviction play that lost 34-33 to Akron. One point. Meanwhile the quietest thing on the board, Miami (OH) -9.5, cruised home 20-3 and asked for no credit.

The published top five went 4-1 for $26.36 and a 52.7 percent ROI, which is a wonderful advertisement for publishing only five things. The other thirty three plays are why the season now reads 239-304-15 over nine real weeks, down $720.10, ROI of negative 12.9 percent. Nineteen lines moved after the picks posted and eleven moved toward the model, which is a lovely way of being right and broke at the same time.
